To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the existence of low lying mesonic states can be understood as a consequence of the confinement potential and that the mass spectra of pseudoscalar and scalar mesons are in agreement with the predictions of the extended Nambus Jona-Lasinio-model.
the existence of low lying meson states is a consequence of confinement and that the confinement potential leads to a stable nonet of vector mesons.

confinement leads to the existence of low lying meson resonances, which can be understood as bound states of quark-antiparticles, and that the confinement potential is responsible for the stability of vector mesons against decays into quarks and antiquarks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic study of low lying hadron masses in QCD with linearly rising potentials.
a systematic investigation of the low lying meson mass spectra within a QCD based approach, which is based on the Bethe-Solpeter equation for mesons in a confining potential.
the investigation of the low-lying meson spectrum in QCD within the Nambu-Jonas-Lasinio model and its generalization to a linearly rising confining potential.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the existence of low lying meson resonances is a consequence of the confinement potential.
the confinement mechanism alone is sufficient to explain the existence of low-lying hadrons as a consequence of QCD.
confinement is the reason for the existence of these low-lying meson nonets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the low-lying meson spectra are consequences of the confinement potential.
the existence of low lying meson nonets is a consequence of the linearly rising potential in QCD.
confinement is responsible for the existence of the lightest mesons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the confinement potential is the key ingredient for the stability of these mesons.
the confinement potential is the origin of the low lying meson spectrum.
the existence of low-lying vector and axial-vector resonances is a consequence of confinement and chiral symmetry breaking.
